summary: Clark County lookout first listed in 1937 and moved in 1954 to Washington County, where it stands as the Salem Fire Tower on private land.

facts.design: Four-leg steel truss tower with a cabin at the top, silver in color
facts.status_note: Not standing at the original Clark County site. Moved in 1954 to a spot about 8 miles north of Salem, Washington County, and now stands as the Salem Fire Tower.
facts.agency: Indiana Department of Conservation, Division of Forestry

access.note: The moved tower stands on private property near Salem, not in a state park or forest. The Indiana Fire Towers author found it standing but not accessible.

visit.trail_note: No public access to the moved tower. No source I could read describes the original Clark County site today.

events.note: Listed among fire warden personnel in the state's 1937 annual report, which implies the tower was standing in July 1937.
National Geodetic Survey description: four-leg steel truss tower with a cabin at the top, about 85 feet high.
Division of Forestry moved the 80-foot tower about 8 miles north of Salem, in Washington County. The announcement is dated August 11, 1954.
Renamed the Salem Fire Tower after the move.
A federal survey note says the tower had been torn down and only footings remained. This conflicts with the 1954 move.
The moved tower, as the Salem Fire Tower, was registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on August 2, 2026.

corrections.why: The tower was moved in 1954 about 8 miles north of Salem and now stands as the Salem Fire Tower. Gone is true only of the original Clark County site.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1947 National Geodetic Survey description says about 85 feet; the 1954 newspaper report and the NHLR entry for the moved tower say 80 feet. The record keeps 24.4 m (80 ft).

A 1966 survey note says the Borden tower was torn down with footings left. The 1954 report, the NHLR entry and the Indiana Fire Towers research all say it was moved. The move is better supported because it has a date and a named receiving site.

notes_for_editor: The Borden record says gone, but the structure was moved in 1954 and is the Salem Fire Tower (us-in-salem, verified). Link the two records. The 1966 federal survey note conflicts with the move and is kept as a dissenting account. No build date and no staffing source were found; 1937 is the earliest dated mention. The Ron Kemnow page was not read directly; its claim is cited through Indiana Fire Towers.
